758103b1282d6b91.title: The case n = 1 for every continuous dimension
758103b1282d6b91.gloss: With one integer coordinate and any continuous dimension \(d\), some point of \(S\) has normalized depth at least \(0.0389\), independent of \(d\). The conjecture therefore holds for \(n = 1\) with \(c_0 = 1/e - (1 - 1/e)\log\frac{e}{e-1} \approx 0.0779\).

daef2580cdfec07b.title: The case n = 2 for every continuous dimension
daef2580cdfec07b.gloss: With two integer coordinates and any \(d\), the conjecture holds unconditionally with \(c_0 = 1/(64e)\). The same argument lifts to any \(n\) whenever the positive-volume fibres over an affine slice of codimension \(r\) span an affine space of dimension at most \(2\).

245739007817b92a.title: Every integer dimension n, every continuous dimension d ≤ 199
245739007817b92a.formula: \forall n\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\ \ \forall d\le 199:\qquad h_S(\mathbf y^\star)\ \ge\ \frac{3}{64000}\,2^{-n}\,\mathcal H_d(S)
245739007817b92a.gloss: The restricted weak Oertel theorem: every \(n\) and every \(d \le 199\) satisfy the locked statement with the absolute constant \(3/64000\). The cap on \(d\) comes from a residual-rank estimate in the hard branch, where a small terminal ledger forces \(d \ge 200\).

9468b734966ba646.title: Bounded intrinsic support rank
9468b734966ba646.gloss: If the positive-volume lattice fibres span an affine space of dimension at most \(R\), the conjecture holds with a constant depending only on \(R\), not on \(n\) or \(d\). Any sequence of bodies defeating every constant must therefore have positive-support rank tending to infinity.

1787daa1dbe3fbb4.title: Cheng-Basu linear threshold
1787daa1dbe3fbb4.gloss: If the projection of \(C\) contains a translate of \(k[-1,1]^n\), the theorem of Cheng and Basu gives one mixed-integer point for which every containing closed halfspace satisfies the displayed bound. Here \(k\) is the box radius. At \(k\ge3e(n+d)\), the normalized depth is at least \(1/(2e)\).

0790372855abe672.title: O((n+d)/n) threshold
0790372855abe672.gloss: For every convex body whose projection contains a translate of \(k[-1,1]^n\), multi-affine rounding gives one mixed-integer point with the displayed depth. Here \(W\) is the total mixed volume and \(\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j\).

95b9903fc7036094.title: Stronger O((n+d)/n) threshold
95b9903fc7036094.gloss: For every convex body whose projection contains a translate of \(R[-1,1]^n\), this radius suffices for one mixed-integer point of depth at least \(\gamma_d2^{-n}W\). For a genuine Minkowski decomposition \(C=K+P\) with nonempty compact convex \(K,P\), the same depth bound holds at \(R\ge(57/14)k/n\), where \(k=\dim\operatorname{aff}(P)\), if the box lies in the projection of \(P\). Here \(W\) is the total mixed volume and \(\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\).

cb0d20326035a553.title: Rigidity and depth for fixed-normal simplex fibres
cb0d20326035a553.gloss: If every fibre is a simplex with fixed facet normals and the \(d\)-th root of fibre volume is affine, then all fibres are homothetic copies of one simplex with affine centre and scale, and the conjecture holds for this class with \(c_0 = 1/(5e)\).

933fa3d0a98a6ce9.title: Conditional closure: an aggregate ledger bound implies the conjecture
933fa3d0a98a6ce9.gloss: If one absolute \(\eta > 0\) makes the six-term terminal ledger \(A(C)\) at least \(\eta Q\) in every small-core instance, the full conjecture follows with \(c_0(\eta)\). The open subgoal hard-branch-labelled-defect-closure asks for exactly this bound.

6b09aae189415c70.title: Canonical labelled product-cloud reduction
6b09aae189415c70.gloss: The hard alternative behind the current frontier. In the small-core branch, either the accepted terminal capacities already total \(Q/100\), or one of two explicit labelled-cloud defects exceeds \(Q/4\). Converting that defect into a capacity is the unresolved step; {usedBy} facts build on this reduction.

a728f1f23a4398e9.title: A least-dimensional counterexample cannot be parity-concentrated
a728f1f23a4398e9.gloss: Structure of a minimal counterexample. If a body violates the constant \(c_{\mathrm{sp}}\) at the least possible base dimension, its canonical stopped set cannot lie in a single parity class: that would cap the intrinsic rank at \(311\) and force the bound after all.

6d6fcf377e68c79c.title: The S-Helly centerpoint theorem
6d6fcf377e68c79c.gloss: For any finite Borel measure carried by a closed set \(S\) with finite \(S\)-Helly number \(h(S)\), some point of \(S\) has depth \(M/h(S)\). For \(\Lambda = \mathbb Z^n \times \mathbb R^d\) this is the Basu–Oertel baseline \(W/(2^n(d+1))\); its decay in \(d\) is what the conjecture asks to remove.

4cfd86cd551df9e7.title: Mixed-continuous volume comparison
4cfd86cd551df9e7.gloss: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body whose projection contains a translate of \(k[-1,1]^n\), with \(k>1/2\), and set \(S_D=D\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\). This compares mixed-integer volume with ordinary volume in both directions and is a shared input to the three highlighted projected-box threshold results.

6769574fc1bd9f8d.title: The metronoid–Grünbaum sandwich
6769574fc1bd9f8d.gloss: Every point of the metronoid \(M_m(K)\), the set of barycentres of sub-bodies of mass \(m\), has fibre depth at least \(\gamma_d\, m\), and conversely every point of depth \(m\) lies in the metronoid. This is the most cited fact in the graph: {usedBy} proofs invoke it.

be359f8a6c628483.title: Dominated-measure residual depth and parity midpoints
be359f8a6c628483.gloss: Any measure dominated by the mixed volume and carried by \(S\) certifies depth, with a bound depending only on its mass, the affine rank \(\rho_\sigma\) of its lattice projection, and its continuous residual rank \(r_\sigma\). The parity-midpoint specialization is cited by {usedBy} facts.

daf10421c94b79ba.title: Cube metronoid mass threshold
daf10421c94b79ba.gloss: For a cube times a convex body, the mixed metronoid contains a point with integral base exactly when the selected mass is at most \(W/2^n\). This is a threshold on selected mass, not on projection radius. The universal \(2^{-n}\) mass factor in the metronoid lifting lemma is sharp.

c168604b1c021192.title: An n = 3 family separating the accepted score mechanisms
c168604b1c021192.gloss: An explicit family in \(\mathbb Z^3 \times \mathbb R^j\) on which every accepted lower-rank, reflection, and slice score is \(o(W)\), yet a full-rank \(1+1+1\) packet still certifies depth above \(W/(8e)\). It refutes any compensation theorem built from those scores without touching the conjecture itself.
